subject: SEM: Error probably due to dummy mispecification

messages.author: f2659346bc7923d6
messages.subject: SEM: Error probably due to dummy mispecification
parts:
Dear All,

This the first time that I've work with categorical values data analysis, and the first time that I use lavaan.

I received this error while I was performing my trial of SEM.

Error in muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  :
  unknown ov.types:factor

This is the part of my script prior the error:

#### Making dummy variables from a case with K > 2 levels ###
# Transforming grown to factor
raw.data$grown <- factor(raw.data$grown, labels = c("1", "2", "3"))
class(raw.data$grown)
str(raw.data) #Inspecting the data set

#the contrast matrix for categorical variable with three levels
contr.treatment(3)
#assigning the treatment contrasts to grown
contrasts(raw.data$grown) = contr.treatment(3)
str(raw.data) #Inspecting the data set

### centering and rescaling numeric explanatory variables ###
prep$lnexp_5y <- scale(prep$lnexp_5y)
prep$age<-scale (prep$age)
prep$yearsliving <-scale (prep$yearsliving)
prep$hourshome <-scale (prep$hourshome)
str(prep)

# Building the model
# The observed variable in black is a dummy.
odor1 <- '
# latent variables (measurement model)
rsi =~ eyes_a + nose_a + run_nose_a +
cough_a + chest_a + breath_a
nsh =~ dizziness_a + concentration_a +
headache_a + fatigue_a + nausea_a
psy =~ risk_perception + behavioral
ap =~ lnexp_5y


sde =~ gender + smoking + grown + children + yearsliving
oa =~ odor_binom

#regressions (dependent ~ independent | y ~ x)
rsi ~ ap + oa
psy ~ ap + oa
nsh ~ ap + oa + psy
oa ~ ap + sde
'
# Fitting the model with WLSMV
fit1.ml <- sem(odor1, data = prep, ordered = c("grown"), estimator = "WLSMV")

Thanks in advance.

Best regards,
Vinícius

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: SEM: Error probably due to dummy mispecification
parts:
lavaan only handles ordered data, not nominal.  If your data conform to this, then when you create factors from dummy codes, use the ordered() function, not the factor() function.

Terry

messages.author: f2659346bc7923d6
messages.subject: Re: SEM: Error probably due to dummy mispecification [Solved]
parts:
Hi Terry,

Thanks a lot.
I could solve the problem with the dummies.

I made it that way:
# Making dummy variables from a case with K > 2 levels
# Transforming grown to factor

prep$grown.f <- factor(prep$grown, labels = c("1", "2", "3"))
tapply(prep$lnexp_5y, prep$grown.f, mean) # Silly checking of the transformation
ido <- sort(unique(prep$grown.f))
contrasts(ido) # Inspecting the binary combinations considering the first level as reference
length(ido)
dg <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(prep), ncol = (length(ido)-1)) #creating empty dummy dataset
dg
d.dim <- (length(ido)-1)
for (j in 1:d.dim) {
  dg[,j] <- as.integer(prep$grown.f == ido[j])
}
dg
prep2 <- cbind(prep, dg)
head(prep2)
prep2$"1" <- as.factor(prep2$"1")
prep2$"2" <- as.factor(prep2$"2")
str(prep2)
names(prep2) <- c("lnexp_5y", "gender", "age",
                     "smoking", "grown", "yearsliving",
                     "children", "hourshome", "job", "odor_binom",
                     "behavioral", "risk_perception",
                     "eyes_a", "nose_a", "run_nose_a", "nausea_a",
                     "cough_a", "chest_a", "breath_a", "fatigue_a",
                     "headache_a", "concentration_a", "dizziness_a",
                     "grown.f", "grown2", "grown3")
prep3 <- prep2
str(prep3)


If anyone has a more efficient way to generate dummies "by hand", please feel free to add to this thread.

Best regards,
Vinícius
On 04/21/2015 07:17 AM, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:

lavaan only handles ordered data, not nominal.  If your data conform to this, then when you create factors from dummy codes, use the ordered() function, not the factor() function.

Terry
